_README: REBASE-BASE FLOORS -- the single, queryable enumeration of every schema/gate/anchor
transition that a rebase base (or a PR head) MUST clear. Consumed by
ci-hub/validate/gate_floors.py (derives the effective floor at call time) and by
ci-hub/validate/preflight_anchor.py (refuses a doomed head before validate starts).
WHY A FLOOR EXISTS. A commit can be fully GREEN and still sit on the WRONG SIDE of a
schema transition. The signature of a floor is a CONSUMER THAT FAILS CLOSED on a
MISSING or NULL field: the field did not exist before some commit, so any head
predating that commit can never satisfy the consumer no matter how green its run.
Two kinds have been observed, IDENTICAL in structure:
* kind=producer-anchor -- the PRODUCER (validate.sh) predating `sha` emits the
required receipt field NULL; the fail-closed certifier rejects every record.
(green-but-null-fielded; a doomed ~17-min validate.)
* kind=merge-gate -- the head predating `sha` validates GREEN yet the merge gate /
branch protection REFUSES the landing (green-but-refused).
THE EFFECTIVE FLOOR = THE NEWEST of these on the branch's first-parent history.
A base must clear ALL floors; clearing the newest clears every older one ONLY when
the newest is a descendant of each older -- gate_floors.py verifies membership on
first-parent history and REFUSES rather than guessing when a floor is off-history or
when GREEN and at-or-after-floor have an empty intersection.
ADD A NEW ENTRY HERE whenever a receipt-schema requirement or a gate version is
tightened to fail closed. Its `sha` is the commit on rrnewton/hermit:main that
introduced the fail-close. Until that commit lands, leave it in `_pending` -- an
entry with a placeholder SHA would refuse every head.
See memory: validate-producer-version-coupled-rebase-before-greening,
merge-gate-v2-floor-invalidates-pre-floor-greens.
